issues.location: hooks/lib/stack-optimizer.sh:73-101 (sb_stack_ensure_agentmemory_gitignore), called from sb_optimize_agentmemory before the wire-consent check
issues.problem: Write outside the project through a repository-controlled symlink. The optimizer touches/greps/appends to "$repo/.gitignore" without checking that it is a regular file inside the project. A cloned repo can commit .gitignore as a symlink (git checks it out with only a warning) to e.g. ../../.bashrc; with nothing more than agentmemory 'enforce' consent the apply appends SB's managed block there. The appended '.agentmemory/*' line is a glob command: in an interactive shell started in the repo it executes the repo's .agentmemory/<first file>. Latent today only because sb-optimize-stack.sh still targets the plugin root (R6-23); H4b is about to point it at the user's project.
issues.evidence: scripts/gitignore-symlink.sh: repo commits '.gitignore -> ../../home-gi/.bashrc_victim' (git ls-files -s: 120000), consent grant agentmemory --project <repo> --capabilities enforce, sb_optimize_agentmemory <repo> -> victim now ends with '# === agentmemory managed block === ... .agentmemory/* ...'. Then with .agentmemory/a.sh in the repo: (cd repo && bash --rcfile victim -i -c true) created PWNED_BASHRC ('PWNED-by-bashrc').
issues.suggested_fix: In sb_stack_ensure_agentmemory_gitignore refuse (print a SKIP/WARN) when .gitignore is a symlink or its physical parent is not the project root (reuse sb_opt_in_path_under / [[ -L ]]), and write by temp file in the project + rename instead of touch/>>/sed -i on the path. Add a hostile-config test with a symlinked .gitignore. Apply the same rule to any other repo path the optimizer writes.

issues.problem: A config query_state_file/usage_state_file may still name any file directly in the runtime state dir, including SB's control files. '${SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR}/trivial' makes a graphify query arm the legacy trivial marker, which disables stop-check, ci-status-check, planning-file-guard and subagent-stop for the session; 'state' would be overwritten by an epoch. A repo can already reach the same Stop bypass via state.trivial_file (core-gate issue, other package), so this is not a new capability, but the containment helper should not allow it.

issues.problem: Read-modify-write without a lock: concurrent grants/declines/revokes lose updates. A lost revoke leaves consent granted after the user (or a script) believed it was removed.
issues.evidence: scripts/conc.sh: 7 parallel 'sb-consent.sh grant <tool> --all-projects --capabilities enforce' -> only 1-2 of 7 recorded in each of 5 rounds.
issues.suggested_fix: Serialize sb_consent_set with a lock in the store directory (mkdir lock with stale recovery, or flock when available), re-reading the store inside the lock.

issues.evidence: scripts/store.sh: ln -s victim consent.json.bak; sb-consent.sh grant alumnium ... -> victim now contains the consent JSON.

issues.problem: The migration notice asks 'Enable <tool> for this project?' and the Yes command ('grant <tool> --project DIR' with default capabilities) also records install and wire for the whole machine. Docs do not say that the store is writable by the governed agent (same OS user) and that consent defends against repository content, not against the agent; deny messages hand the agent a one-line 'decline' command without 'only when the user asks'. 'sb-consent.sh --project' does not resolve a subdirectory to the SB project root, so 'grant --project .' from src/ silently records a key no gate reads.
issues.evidence: scripts/ss.sh notice text; consent grant graphify --project <proj> prints 'install=granted, wire=granted, enforce=granted' and the store has machine.graphify.install/wire; key.sh: key for <proj>/src is <proj>/src.

issues.problem: macOS Bash 3.2 with set -u: '"${arr[@]}"' on an empty array is an unbound-variable error. sb_rt_state_file reaches it when the configured path is exactly '${SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR}/' (rel empty), so the stamp path becomes empty (the subshell dies) and the gate can never be satisfied; _sb_opt_in_program reaches it for a command starting with an operator. Not reproducible here (only Bash 5.2 installed); static reasoning.
issues.evidence: Static: IFS=/ read -r -a _sb_rt_parts <<<"" yields an empty array; Bash < 4.4 errors on "${_sb_rt_parts[@]}" under nounset; hooks run with set -euo pipefail.
issues.suggested_fix: Guard with [[ -n "$rel" ]] / ${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"} and add a Bash-3.2-safe test (empty rel falls back).

issues.problem: The end-to-end 'a version string is never evaluated' assertions use HOSTILE='a[$(touch ...)]'. Under set -u an unset name 'a' aborts before its subscript is evaluated, so the original vulnerable comparison ([[ have -ge $min ]]) would not run the command either: the assertions cannot fail. (Value-level validation tests in test-rtk-gate-coverage.sh / test-context-mode-libs-coverage.sh do catch removal of the validators.) Similarly the R5-04 'recommendation without consent never blocks' loop is short-circuited by the prelude's no-store check, so it does not exercise sb_recommended_tool_enforced.
issues.evidence: Sandbox mutation M4 (sb_rt_version_ge -> [[ "${have%%.*}" -ge "$min" ]], validators removed): hostile-config 31/0. Same mutation with HOSTILE changed to 'HOME[$(touch ...)]': 29/2 ('hostile min_version / min_node_version ran a command', 'the diagnostics entry points evaluated it'); unmutated code with HOME[...] 31/0. Mutation M2 (consent from config) leaves hostile-config 31/0; only test-recommended-tools-coverage.sh 'not enforced without user consent' fails.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a set variable (HOME[$(touch ...)]) as the original probe did, and add a hostile-config case where the store records consent for a different project/tool so the gate reaches sb_recommended_tool_enforced.
